ssgb_guide.text: Welcome aboard the SS Great Britain! This is the first-class dining saloon. White and gold, pillars, mirrors: very swish.
When she was launched in 1843 she was the longest ship in the world, and the first big iron ship with a propeller to cross the Atlantic.
Down below, the dry dock's sealed under a glass 'sea' so you can walk under her hull. Dry air keeps the old iron from rusting away.

then.text: Back to Temple Meads with that notebook! Prudence will want to hear all about it.
Brunel's notebook? Page two: 'Great Britain. Iron hull. Screw propeller.' He changed his mind from paddle wheels halfway through building her.
Paddles were the old way. A screw propeller sits under the water, out of harm's way. The navy took note, I can tell you.
There, the ship's stamp. Off to Temple Meads to finish the trail.

else.text: Brunel's notebook! But you've skipped a page. Start at the bridge, up the gorge. Brunel would want it done in order.
